title: The same workload targets both user and device groups

report.title: {Items.Count} {Plural(Items.Count, 'object mixes', 'objects mix')} user and device targeting

messages.businessImpact: Behaviour varies by whether a person or a machine matched first, which makes support cases hard to reproduce and harder to explain.
remediation: Choose one targeting model per object and apply it consistently.
messages.cannotSee: What a group holds is worked out from its members rather than from anything Entra declares, because Entra has no such property: a group is whatever has ended up in it. A group whose membership this run could not read settles nothing and is passed over, so an object is never reported on the strength of a group nobody could see, and an empty group is passed over too. Anything that is neither a device nor a nested group counts towards people, so a group of service principals reads as a user group. Mixing may also be deliberate, since an application offered to users and required on kiosks is one object doing two jobs.
